author: Jian Shao, Sensen Wu, Yixuan Chen, Jin Qi, Yijun Chen, Minlong Huang, Feng Wu, Lian Feng, Chengfeng Le, Renyi Liu, Zhenhong Du

title: Range-Dependent Folded Clutter Suppression for IPPAW-Based Side-Looking Airborne Radar in Nonhomogeneous Environments
content: Side-looking airborne radar (SLAR) systems employing conventional waveforms suffer from range ambiguity, whereby near-range clutter is folded into the same range segment as far-range low-velocity target echoes, thereby degrading target detection performance. In nonhomogeneous environments, range-folded moving discrete clutter and background clutter affected by internal clutter motion (ICM) further complicate clutter suppression. To address these problems, a range-dependent folded clutter suppression algorithm is developed for interpulse phase agile waveform (IPPAW)-based SLAR systems. The proposed algorithm first establishes an accurate clutter representation through clutter-model calibration and the construction of an ICM-aware block dictionary. Using this representation together with the range-segment-dependent slow-time modulation introduced by IPPAW, the algorithm estimates the corresponding range-dependent clutter supports and constructs an orthogonal projection matrix for folded clutter suppression. The diversity introduced by IPPAW also alleviates the folding effect of moving discrete clutter in far-range target segments. Simulated and measured data processing results show that the proposed algorithm achieves effective range-dependent folded clutter suppression, leading to improved suppression of nonhomogeneous folded clutter and enhanced detection of far-range low-velocity targets.
author: Zihao Liu, Huayu Fan, Shaoqiang Chang, Quanhua Liu, Lixiang Ren, Erke Mao

title: Patch-to-Channel Adaptive Graph Upsampling for Pan-Sharpening
content: Although deep learning has achieved remarkable success in pan-sharpening, the prevalent upsampling algorithms often neglect critical cross-modal information from panchromatic (PAN) images and global structural details from low-resolution multispectral images, thereby significantly constraining the quality of the reconstructed high-resolution multispectral image. To alleviate these issues, we introduce a patch-to-channel adaptive graph upsampling (PCAGU) module, which progressively models relationships at both patch and channel levels through graph-based learning. Specifically, the PCAGU module first leverages a patch-based graph neural network (GNN) to capture long-range structural relationships, where an adaptive similarity construction, enhanced by task-oriented row normalization, ensures stable and similarity-aware feature aggregation. Subsequently, a channel-based GNN is employed to facilitate cross-channel spectral interactions, effectively enhancing spectral consistency while maintaining high-fidelity spatial structures. Furthermore, as a lightweight and plug-and-play module, PCAGU can be seamlessly integrated into diverse pan-sharpening frameworks. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets show that the proposed PCAGU consistently boosts various baseline networks, achieving superior quantitative performance and visual fidelity, while providing a favorable tradeoff between reconstruction accuracy and computational efficiency compared with existing learnable PAN-guided upsampling methods.
author: Shutong Duan, Kai Sun, Xiaoyue Xie, Jiangshe Zhang, Zengjie Song, Xiangyong Cao

title: Georegistration of Terrestrial LiDAR Point Clouds With Satellite Images Without GNSS
content: Accurate georegistration of LiDAR point clouds remains challenging in urban environments where Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals are denied or degraded. Existing methods often depend on real-time GNSS and inertial measurement unit (IMU) data requiring precalibration and stable signals. We propose a structured post-hoc map-referenced georegistration method for terrestrial LiDAR point clouds using public road-map references. It targets LiDAR-only or GNSS-degraded urban maps where field-surveyed control points, RTK-GNSS, total stations, or official geodetic products are unavailable, costly, or impractical. Rather than replacing survey-grade georeferencing, it provides a low-cost, scalable postprocessing route for road-dominant, map-covered urban and urban-suburban environments. A pretrained Point Transformer segments road points, from which road skeletons and intersections are extracted in both modalities. Global rigid alignment using corresponding intersections is followed by local nonrigid refinement with radial basis function interpolation. The vertical component is treated as optional coarse terrain anchoring using Shuttle Radar Topography Mission data. Evaluation measures road-level map consistency and includes independent validation with OSM, Mapbox, and HERE. On KITTI, the method achieves a mean planimetric alignment error of 0.69 m and improves over the raw KITTI GNSS annotations. On the Perth dataset, it achieves 2.17 m on the primary Google-based reference while remaining consistent across independent map providers. Elevation correlation improves from 0.59 to 0.77 on KITTI and from 0.38 to 0.86 on Perth. Code, corrected datasets, and a demonstration video are publicly available.
author: Xinyu Wang, Muhammad Ibrahim, Haitian Wang, Atif Mansoor, Xiuping Jia, Ajmal Mian

title: Ship Detection for SAR Images Based on 0-Dimensional Topological Persistent Homology and Local Density-Suppression Diffusion Model
content: Existing synthetic aperture radar (SAR) ship detection methods often have difficulties in complex environments with strong speckle noise, multipeak intensity distributions, and prominent sidelobes. To address the problem, we propose a framework that combines zeroth-dimensional (0-D) persistent homology (PH) with a local density-suppression diffusion model. First, an exponential Perona–Malik anisotropic diffusion smoothes the image while preserving structure, creating an energy field that reduces noise and retains target edges. Second, 0-D PH measures the stability of connected structures in a superlevel-set sequence of the energy field. Finally, a density-informed diffusion process protects high-density target regions and suppresses low-density residual scatterers, further isolating ships. Experiments on AIR-SARShip-1.0, FAIR-CSAR-1.0, RSDD-SAR, and SSDD demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method across low-intensity homogeneous backgrounds, strong noise, multipeak distributions, multitarget scenes, strong sidelobes, and complex inshore environments. The six-scene macro averages of the proposed method are 0.9053 for F1-score and 0.1140 for FDR.
author: Hongyu Long, Chun Liu, Bofei Fu, Jian Yang

title: A Dual-Polarization-Integrated Time-Series InSAR Framework for Arc-Level Parameter Estimation and Network Densification
content: Conventional time-series synthetic aperture radar interferometry (InSAR) techniques often suffer from temporal decorrelation and limited coherent-point density when relying on single-polarization data. This study develops a dual-polarization-integrated polarimetric time-series InSAR framework that connects established polarization-optimized persistent scatterer candidate selection with dual-polarization arc-level model-parameter estimation. At the point-selection stage, established exhaustive search polarimetric optimization and an signal-to-noise ratio (SNR)-parameterized alternating search are adopted to minimize the amplitude dispersion index of dual-polarization (VV/VH) data. The principal methodological extension is the direct incorporation of polarization projection into arc-level deformation-parameter estimation through two implementations, temporal coherence optimization and SNR-parameterized alternating arc-level optimization. Both jointly estimate polarization and phase-model parameters by maximizing residual temporal coherence and are compared with PEAK and weighted-sum multipolarization model parameter optimization. Using 45 dual-polarization Sentinel-1 A images covering Jieyang Chaoshan International Airport, the tested configurations show that the arc-level implementations increase the availability of high-coherence arcs. The resulting point–arc constraints subsequently support a denser final PS network, including additional quality-controlled isolated points, while the retrieved deformation fields exhibit improved spatial continuity and internal consistency. Network densification and isolated-point recovery are therefore treated as downstream outcomes rather than as independent optimization objectives.
author: Guoming Xie, Alex Hay-Man Ng, Jianfei Wang, Kui Zhang, Hua Wang

title: Robust Reconstruction of ISAR Scattering Center Based on Coherent Scattering-Structure Representation
content: High-precision reconstruction of scattering centers is central to remote sensing interpretation and ISAR diagnostics, yet in low-SNR scenarios, coherent signal responses degrade so severely that reliable parameter estimation becomes fundamentally compromised. This article develops a robust ISAR scattering-center reconstruction framework based on RD-domain coherent scattering-structure representation (CSSR). The proposed method is oriented toward structured parameter extraction rather than visual image enhancement. First, an echo-domain ESPRIT preprocessing stage is introduced only for robust candidate initialization, so that dominant spectral components are stabilized under strong disturbance. Second, a CSSR model is established directly in the RD image domain, where localized and line-distributed scattering mechanisms can be jointly described by analytically tractable atoms with clear spatial geometry and coherent phase. Third, the reconstruction task is formulated as a global RD-domain residual projection problem. Candidate structures are selected from residual peaks and ESPRIT priors, refined in continuous coordinates, reprojected by regularized orthogonal least squares, and stopped using a noise-adaptive threshold. Comparative experiments with existing typical methods, based on electromagnetic calculation data and anechoic chamber measurement data, demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the scattering center reconstruction using the method proposed in this article.
author: Hanjie Wu, Yongqiang Cheng, Kang Liu, Runming Zou, Runzhou Li

title: End-to-End Evolving Cross-Modal Graph Network for Unsupervised Multimodal Remote Sensing Change Detection
content: Unsupervised multimodal change detection aims to detect surface changes from heterogeneous remote sensing imagery without labeled data, enabling timely and reliable monitoring in dynamic environments. Existing graph-based unsupervised multimodal change detection methods rely on static graph priors, which cannot be optimized end-to-end. To address these limitations, we propose evolving cross-modal graph network, an unsupervised framework consisting of a structure evolving graph embedding module and a cross-modal graph generalization module. The structure evolving graph embedding module dynamically constructs latent evolving graph representations by implicitly learning node relationships through a learnable affinity kernel and a discrete graph integral operator, enabling progressive graph evolution under end-to-end optimization. The cross-modal graph generalization module refines the latent evolving graph representation by enforcing intramodality reconstruction and cross-modality consistency loss, where a distribution-conditioned transformation operator aligns the statistical distribution to produce modality-invariant features and reduce sensor bias. Extensive experiments were conducted on four benchmark datasets and a large-scale Wangjiaba flood dataset. Results show that ECG-Net outperforms state-of-the-art methods for robust unsupervised multimodal change detection.
author: Chaoyi Wang, Dingyuan Chen, Xinyi Gong, Hongbo Wang, Zhaohui Song

title: The High-Accuracy InSAR PWV Retrieval Methods Based on Machine-Learning Fusing Multisource Data
content: High-accuracy, high-spatial-resolution precipitable water vapor (PWV) is essential for severe weather observation and prediction. Although interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) can provide PWV information at fine spatial resolution, its retrieval accuracy is poor. Most existing methods optimize InSAR PWV using global navigation satellite system or ERA5 PWV. However, performance improvements remain limited, and effectiveness in regions with complex topography still requires further validation. Therefore, Kunming and its surrounding areas in Yunnan Province, China, with complex topography, are selected as the study area. First, differential zenith tropospheric delay (ΔZTD) was extracted from the Sentinel-1A time series using small baseline subset-InSAR. Then, two models were established: the direct fusion mapping model (DFMM) and the stagewise correction refinement model (SCRM) with physical processes. Both models employed a backpropagation neural network to retrieve ΔPWV by integrating InSAR ΔZTD, continuous operational reference system (CORS) ZTD, CORS PWV, ERA5 PWV, surface pressure, air temperature, and geopotential. Finally, absolute PWV was recovered by adding ERA5 PWV at the reference epoch to the retrieved ΔPWV. The results indicate that, compared with the original InSAR ΔPWV with a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 11.72 mm, the RMSE decreased to 2.29 mm for DFMM and 2.02 mm for SCRM. Both models’ RMSE improvement rates exceed 80%. In the time series, the retrieved DFMM and SCRM PWV show high consistency with the CORS PWV, with R values exceeding 0.94. Spatially, the retrieved DFMM PWV and SCRM PWV show an R of 0.97 with ERA5 PWV and reveal more detailed PWV information. The proposed models achieve high spatial resolution and high accuracy in InSAR PWV retrieval over complex topography, providing high-spatial-resolution PWV datasets to support refined meteorological analysis and related applications.
author: Yiyang Zhao, Xiongwei Ma, Qi Zhang, Youkun Wang, Bao Zhang, Yunzheng Huang, Xiuguang Yao, Yibin Yao, Xiaohu Lin, Wanqiang Yao

title: A Hierarchical Feature Assembly and Adaptive Enhancement Network for Remote Sensing Image Change Detection
content: Change detection (CD) in remote sensing images plays a critical role in urban monitoring, land-use analysis, and disaster assessment. However, existing methods still struggle with insufficient local structure representation, inconsistent deep semantics, and ineffective cross-layer feature fusion, leading to false detections in complex scenes. To address these issues, we propose AssemCD, a hierarchical feature assembly network with adaptive enhancement for remote sensing image CD. Specifically, a Hierarchical Context Assembly Module (HCAM) is designed to integrate local convolutional representation with linear context modeling, enabling unified local-global feature learning. An Adaptive Dual-path Module (ADM) is further introduced to enhance directional consistency in shallow layers and improve multiscale local structure representation. In addition, a Semantic Recalibration Fusion Module (SRFM) is employed to adaptively recalibrate deep features via lightweight global semantic guidance, thereby improving semantic consistency during cross-layer fusion. Experiments on the LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and SYSU-CD datasets demonstrate that AssemCD achieves competitive CD performance. On LEVIR-CD, AssemCD obtains a changed-class IoU of 70.82% and an F1 score of 82.92%, achieving the highest IoU, F1 score, and Kappa coefficient among the compared methods. On WHU-CD, it achieves a changed-class IoU of 63.79% and an F1 score of 77.89%, demonstrating competitive foreground discrimination performance. Under the fixed 25% SYSU-CD sampling protocol, AssemCD achieves a changed-class IoU of 62.73%, an F1 score of 77.09%, and a Kappa coefficient of 70.29%. Ablation experiments further verified the effectiveness and complementarity of HCAM, ADM, and SRFM in hierarchical feature modeling. The complexity analysis indicates that AssemCD is not designed to minimize the parameter count; instead, it achieves competitive detection accuracy under a moderate computational budget.
author: Chen Sirui, Xie Yuhan, Lv Fen, Xie Tao

title: DeCoF: Tiny Object Detection in Aerial Remote Sensing Imagery via Detail-Retentive Downsampling and Conflict-Aware Fusion
content: Aerial object detection has witnessed remarkable progress, yet detecting tiny objects in remote sensing imagery remains highly challenging due to their extremely limited spatial footprints. Hierarchical feature processing pipelines tend to exacerbate this problem, as their standard spatial downsampling operators discard fragile structural cues, while cross-scale fusion often overlooks the representational inconsistency between shallow details and deep contextual priors. To address these bottlenecks, we propose DeCoF for tiny object detection in aerial imagery via two complementary modules. First, we introduce the detail-retentive downsampling (DRD) module, which performs spatial downsampling through polyphase decomposition followed by detail re-encoding. Equipped with learnable structure-preserving shrinkage and a residual-guided update mechanism, DRD suppresses background clutter while alleviating the distortion of fragile object cues. Second, we present the conflict-aware fusion (CAF) module, which explicitly measures the representational inconsistency between shallow details and deep contextual priors to guide cross-scale fusion. Specifically, CAF quantifies such discrepancies via Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, dynamically highlighting ambiguous regions and selectively enhancing complementary contextual priors for more effective multiscale feature aggregation. Extensive experiments on the VisDrone2019 and AI-TOD benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed DeCoF. Specifically, on the VisDrone2019 benchmark, integrating DeCoF yields absolute improvements of 1.7 points in mAP$_{50}$ and 1.6 points in mAP$_{\text{S}}$ over the pre-trained YOLOv9 baseline, and 2.0 points in mAP$_{50}$ and 1.6 points in mAP$_{\text{S}}$ over the RT-DETR baseline. Furthermore, on the AI-TOD dataset, the RT-DETR-based DeCoF achieves 51.1% in mAP$_{50}$ and 22.1% in mAP$_{\text{S}}$. These consistent gains across both CNN-based and transformer-based detectors further verify the paradigm-agnostic nature of DeCoF.
author: Yongjia Wang, Wangyuan Li, Chao Gao, Xianghua Li, Xiao Yang

title: Urban LiDAR Point Cloud Segmentation Using Multilevel Stacked Learning With Counterfactual Guided Minority Class Enhancement
content: Urban LiDAR point cloud segmentation remains a challenging task due to high scene complexity, class imbalance, varying point densities, and noise inherent in real-world datasets. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a multilevel stacked ensemble learning architecture for urban LiDAR point cloud segmentation that enhances segmentation performance. The proposed architecture integrates three hierarchical levels of classifiers: Tree-based ensemble models at the first level, neural network–based classifier at the second level, and a tree-based metaclassifier at the final level to produce refined predictions. Experimental results on two benchmark urban datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches, achieving accuracy and F1-scores exceeding 97% and 92%, respectively, on the high-density Toronto-3D dataset, and 92% and 86%, respectively, on the low-density Vaihingen dataset. Furthermore, this study incorporates SHAP Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) and counterfactual analysis to identify highly sensitive and low-contributing features that contribute to performance degradation in minority classes. By refining the initial input feature set through the exclusion of most sensitive and low-contribution features and subsequently retraining the model, the proposed architecture achieves significantly improved performance for structurally informative minority classes, resulting in a higher F1-score.
author: Debobrata Chakraborty, Ahmed Adnan, Emon Kumar Dey

title: Road-Debris Detection Using Differential-Phase Contrast in W-Band SAR
content: Road debris on roadways and airport runways poses significant hazards, thereby necessitating reliable monitoring. Various sensors, such as camera, LiDAR, and radar, have been employed for debris detection, among which a W-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system based on a 77 GHz frequency-modulated continuous wave radar has attracted increasing attention. Nevertheless, road debris with small size and low radar reflectivity is challenging to detect, as it is indistinguishable from the background in the SAR intensity image. In this study, we propose a road-debris-detection approach based on differential-phase contrast (DPC). DPC denotes the contrast in the differential phase between elevated debris and the surrounding ground surface. Since this contrast arises from height differences, DPC-based detection is less directly dependent on target-to-background intensity contrast than the conventional SAR intensity-based detection, thereby improving the separability of low radar cross-sectional (RCS) debris. A W-band SAR system for road-debris detection was constructed, and a DPC-based detection framework combining differential-phase-based detection with SAR intensity-based detection was proposed. The detection experiments were conducted on seven types of debris with diverse materials and shapes, including debris with low RCS. Compared with the conventional SAR intensity-based method, the proposed DPC-based detection framework achieved precision, recall, and F1-score of 77.78%, 100%, and 87.50%, respectively, representing improvements of 69.94, 42.86, and 73.71 percentage points. The debris-region differential phase exhibited an average contrast-to-noise ratio of 3.135, which was 2.829 higher than that of the intensity image, confirming that the height-induced DPC provides substantially stronger target-to-background contrast. This enhanced contrast enabled reliable detection of low-RCS road debris under the experimental conditions, demonstrating the effectiveness of height-induced DPC as a discriminative feature.
author: Hyokbeen Lee, Duk-jin Kim, Sangho An, Sohee Park, Junwoo Kim

title: Self-Supervised Learning for Very High-Resolution Forest Mapping With TanDEM-X InSAR Data
content: Deep learning models have shown encouraging capabilities for mapping forests at medium resolution with X-band TanDEM-X bistatic interferometric synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data, being able to generate accurate forest/nonforest maps at global scale. Such models, as most of current state-of-the-art deep learning techniques in remote sensing, are trained in a fully supervised way, which requires a large amount of labeled data for training and validation. In this work, our objective is to take advantage of the high-resolution capabilities of the TanDEM-X mission for mapping forests using deep learning, with an unprecedented resolution down to only 6 m. To cope with the lack of extended reliable reference datasets at such a high resolution, we investigate the use of self-supervised learning for extracting highly informative representations from the input features, followed by a supervised downstream task of forest mapping using a significantly smaller amount of reliable labels. The end-to-end framework is first developed over Pennsylvania, USA, thanks to the availability of a high-resolution, LiDAR-based reference map. Here, we verify that self-supervised learning approaches outperform fully supervised learning strategies when using less than 10% of the labeled samples. Building on these findings, we then extend the framework to the Amazon rainforest, where only very few high resolution labeled data are available. In this challenging scenario, the proposed self-supervised framework significantly improves classification accuracy with respect to fully supervised methods, trained using the same amount of labeled data, with increasing the F$_{1}-$score by 24%. In this work, for the first time, self-supervised learning is applied to bistatic interferometric SAR data for forest mapping at 6 m resolution, overcoming the scarcity of annotated labels for training at such a high spatial resolution. The proposed deep-learning-based method is easily scalable and suitable for the generation of large-sale forest mapping products from TanDEM-X data at an unprecedented resolution, paving the way for the development of an operational framework for mapping forest coverage and related changes over the entire pantropics.
author: José-Luis Bueso-Bello, Benjamin Chauvel, Daniel Carcereri, Philipp Posovszky, Pietro Milillo, Jennifer Ruiz, Juan-Carlos Fernández-Diaz, Carolina González, Michele Martone, Ronny Hänsch, Paola Rizzoli

title: Leveraging High-Resolution LISS IV Data and Machine Learning for Land Use Land Cover Mapping: A Comprehensive Workflow and Model Interpretation
content: Satellite remote sensing data are the primary source for land use land cover (LULC) mapping. Developing LULC mapping models using linear imagine self-scanning system IV (LISS IV) data has been rarely explored because of its low spectral resolution (three bands), even though the dataset was made freely accessible in late 2023. This article develops a comprehensive workflow for LULC mapping using LISS IV imagery with 5.8-m spatial resolution, acquired in February 2021 and covering northern Bengaluru, India. Ground-truth data were collected for seven LULC classes. This article explored how machine-learning (ML) models trained on LISS IV data performed across different cross-validation (CV) processes, how to interpret the developed models, and how to evaluate model uncertainty when applied to unseen areas. Three ML models (random forest, extreme gradient boosting—XGB, and light gradient boosting) were compared using random and spatial CV procedures. To enhance the reliability and interpretability of feature attributions, an ensemble-based uncertainty analysis was conducted to quantify epistemic uncertainty within Shapley Additive exPlanations. The uncertainty of the predicted LULC values was evaluated using the dissimilarity index and the area-of-applicability concept. Results showed similar performance across all ML models, with XGB selected for further analysis. The model was further tested on unseen image regions, where 90.5% of pixels were predicted without uncertainty. This article demonstrates the feasibility of using LISS IV data for LULC mapping and highlights the importance of selecting appropriate CV techniques, ensuring interpretability, and integrating explainability and uncertainty quantification to enhance the reliability of ML-based classification.
author: Satya Prakash, Michael Wachendorf, Sunil Nautiyal, Jayan Wijesingha

title: Multisensor Change Detection in Flood Monitoring: A Reliability-Aware Dual-Regularized Fusion Network
content: Change detection (CD) from bitemporal remote sensing images is essential for flood disaster assessment. Recent advancements in Earth observation have enabled multisensor CD (MSCD) to exploit the complementarity of heterogeneous data sources, such as synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and multispectral (MS) images. However, flood-related MSCD remains challenging because flood events introduce reliability imbalance between SAR and MS observations, local feature inconsistencies, and the representation bottleneck encountered in multimodal learning. To tackle these challenges, this article proposes a dual-regularized SAR-guided fusion network. The framework leverages the structural stability of SAR features to adaptively refine MS feature representations, enabling reliability-aware multimodal fusion. To mitigate flood-induced local feature inconsistencies caused by dynamic surface variations, a motion-aware feature enhancement module is designed to enhance bitemporal feature representations. In addition, a dual self-supervised regularization strategy is introduced to balance multimodal semantic consistency with information preservation. Moreover, five representative MSCD architectural paradigms are standardized to support systematic evaluation and comparison. Experiments on a public multisensor dataset and four cross-regional flood scenarios demonstrate the effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed method.
author: Yankun Huang, Zhiguo Liang, Jiaojiao Tian, Yun Zhang

title: DEM Resolution Drives AI Variability: Tradeoffs Between Performance and Explainability in Landslide Susceptibility Prediction
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) has shown strong predictive capability in landslide susceptibility prediction (LSP), but its closed-box nature creates a trust gap in geohazard decision support, where predictive accuracy alone is insufficient. High-resolution digital elevation models (DEMs) are commonly expected to improve terrain representation and prediction, yet it remains unclear whether finer DEMs also improve explanation reliability. This study investigates the resolution-dependent mismatch between predictive performance and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based explanation reliability in AI-based LSP. A 1 m Gaofen-7 DEM was used as the reference and resampled to 5, 10, 12.5, 30, and 90 m. To isolate DEM-resolution effects, the slope-unit layer, landslide labels, and DEM-derived input-factor types were kept consistent across resolutions. Logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and XGBoost were evaluated under repeated random seeds. A quantitative SHAP-based framework integrating faithfulness, stability, and geomorphic consistency was further used to assess explanation reliability. The results show that finer DEMs, especially the 1 m DEM, generally improved classification performance and mapping efficiency. However, this predictive gain did not lead to a synchronous improvement in explanation reliability. Faithfulness was largely insensitive to DEM resolution, whereas stability and geomorphic consistency showed resolution- and model-dependent responses. Coarser DEMs could reduce attribution sensitivity through terrain smoothing, but this apparent stability could be accompanied by shifts in feature-importance structure, especially at 90 m and for LR/SVM, where attribution moved from slope-related information toward broader roughness proxies. Among the tested models, RF showed comparatively strong predictive performance and more stable attribution patterns. These findings show that finer DEMs improve predictive performance but do not necessarily improve explanation reliability. DEM-resolution selection should therefore be treated as an objective-dependent tradeoff rather than being guided by the assumption that finer resolution is always preferable.
